meta.selection: Re-ranked for an engineering applicant. Union of every school ranked by any source; score = best percentile across sources (position in the source's US list / list length; regional lists within region). Always kept: every school ranked by usnNational, forbes, qs, qsEngTech, usnEngDoctorate, usnEngNoDoctorate, except a liberal arts college (U.S. News LAC list) without an engineering bachelor’s; a liberal arts college with one is always kept. The rest fill up to 1000: schools with an engineering bachelor’s first, each group in score order (508 trimmed). Graduate-only institutions are left out.

fields.engBachelors: awards at least 10 Engineering (CIP 14.xx) bachelor’s degrees a year (Scorecard field-of-study; filters out 3-2 dual-degree artifacts) OR has an ABET EAC-accredited bachelor’s program
fields.engDegrees: engineering bachelor’s degrees per year (mean of the 2 award years reported)
fields.engFields: the CIP 14 programs, most graduates first
fields.csBachelors: awards at least 10 Computer Science (CIP 11.07) bachelor’s degrees a year
fields.abetPrograms: ABET EAC-accredited bachelor’s engineering programs (null = none listed)
fields.lac: on the U.S. News liberal arts list (that rank is not shown)
fields.sat: EBRW 25th + Math 25th, EBRW 75th + Math 75th (Scorecard gives section percentiles; the sum approximates the composite)
fields.netPrice: average net price, Title IV students (NPT4_PUB / NPT4_PRIV)
fields.ranks: integer rank (a band's lower bound); rankLabels holds the printed form for ties ("=12") and bands ("801-850")
fields.score: best percentile across sources (lower is better); selection key
fields.rounds: published admit rate per round {ed, ed2, ea, rd}: {rate (percent as printed), year (fall of entry), src (URL)}; a round with no published rate is absent; never computed; newest year wins, same year: school-published, then Summit Prep, then College Transitions; in-state / out-of-state rows ignored
